# Publishing {#sec-publishing}

As detailed in the original project description to the Novo Nordisk Foundation
(<https://dp-next.github.io/>) and Section 12 of the collaboration agreement, we
aim to work, collaborate, and publish following the principles of open and
reproducible science.

Briefly, the collaboration agreement states that the [Steering
Committee](https://dp-next.github.io/who-we-are.html) is responsible for
outlining and implementing the project's publication strategy. The main aims of
this strategy are:

- To jointly publish positive, negative, and inconclusive results in
  international peer-reviewed scientific journals.
- To work according to open and reproducible research practices.

::: callout-note
In case of any fundamental discrepancy or conflict between this page and the
collaboration agreement, the text of the collaboration agreement has precedence.
If any substantial deviations from this guide are needed for a particular
research project, the authors should justify the deviations and request approval
to proceed from the Steering Committee.
:::

So, how do we put this strategy into practice? When a scientific output is ready
to be disseminated, either "informally" (in archives like Zenodo) or "formally"
in journals or other channels, in DP-Next we follow a specific path. See
@fig-publication-steps below for the basics of this path, with later sections
describing things in more detail.

## When new results are ready to be published

'New results' means any results that have not yet been formally published in a
peer-reviewed journal. Results included in a conference abstract/presentation,
preprint, or GitHub repository are still considered new results until they are
formally published. When disseminating new results, follow these tasks:

- Including preliminary or new results in lectures or seminars that is outside
  of DP-Next should be done with care. Researchers wishing to present new
  results in small academic circles should notify the Steering Committee before
  giving the presentation, by raising an issue in the research project's GitHub
  (or in the WP1-Management repository).

- You can only disseminating new results through media or outreach activities
  after disseminating the results in the form of a published conference abstract
  or presentation. In the case of a press release related to the conference, you
  can prepare the dissemination beforehand under a time embargo that coincides
  with the academic presentation of results.

- Before issuing any press release or disseminating any new results from
  DP-Next, researchers should inform the Steering Committee via an issue on the
  (private) WP1-Management repo. You should do this as early as possible. If
  approval is needed in less than 72 hours, send an e-mail to or call one of the
  members of Steering Committee.

- After the dissemination activity is done, you should send a copy or link to
  the final materials to the Steering Committee and report/log the activity on
  the project's GitHub.

## General disseminating activities

If you want to disseminate something that is generally about DP-Next or on
already published results (i.e. not including preliminary results, preprints,
conference abstracts or GitHub content), you don't need approval from the
Steering Committee. But it is still appreciated if you keep us informed, via the
Discord channel or making an issue on WP1-Management with details about the
dissemination activity.

These other forms of dissemination include: keynotes, invited talks, press
releases, media appearances, podcasts, posts on social media, or outreach
activities. In general, dissemination activities must never interfere with or
weaken the opportunities for academic publication of the study results.
